newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bridgestone sees modest rubber easing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bridgestone sees modest rubber easing.

text.p: Tyre manufacturer Bridgestone Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it expected some further modest easing in natural rubber prices in the second half of 1996.
Bridgestone chairman Deane Jarvis said the price of rubber had been coming off gradually throughout the first half of 1996, although it did not fall as quickly as the company had hoped.
"I think we are expecting some further modest easing in rubber prices in the second half," he told Reuters.
Bridgestone earlier announced a rise of 2.8 percent in total sales to A$218.7 million and a 2.4 percent rise in pre-tax operating profit to A$9.8 million for the first half of the year to June 30.

Jarvis said Bridgestone's results had been adversely affected, especially in 1995 and the second half of 1994, by a rapid increase in the cost of natural rubber, caused by seasonal conditions and strong demand from China and the United States.
"As far as I am aware there have not been any unusual seasonal conditions which have affected the position this year, and I think demand has remained strong, but not abnormally strong," Jarvis said.
He said the company did not publicly release its rubber purchase figures.
The company's supply channels were secure, procuring in conjunction with parent Bridgestone Corp 5108., he said.
Bridgestone Corp owns about 60 percent of Bridgestone Australia.
